title: Runtime telemetry sampling and cost-aware profiling policy
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines Redwood's standardized policy for runtime telemetry sampling and cost-aware profiling. It describes which signals to collect, how to sample requests to meet SLOs while controlling telemetry costs, recommended storage/retention tiers, and an operational runbook for changes or incidents that require higher-fidelity traces. The goal is to preserve diagnostic signal for engineering and SRE workflows while bounding observability costs and avoiding unbounded ingestion/ingress spikes.

Motivation and goals
--------------------
- Reduce observability spend growth while retaining high utility for performance and regression investigations.
- Provide deterministic, auditable sampling behavior across runtime components (dispatcher, kernel dispatcher, kvcache, model-handler).
- Make profiling decisions workload-aware: bursty clients, tail-heavy routes, canary experiments, and high-cost model variants should get more coverage.
- Define safe escalation and rollback paths when increased telemetry is required during incidents or experiments.

Telemetry signals (priority list)
--------------------------------
1) High-value, low-volume (always-on)
   - Per-request SLO metadata: request_id, route, model_variant, tenant, priority_class, latency_ms, status_code
   - Aggregated token-level counters: tokens_requested, tokens_emitted per model_variant (1s rollup)
2) Medium-value (sampled)
   - Traces for inference lifecycle across runtime components (dispatcher -> kernel -> device)
   - Kernel queue times and kernel execution durations (p50/p95/p99 histograms)
3) Low-value / expensive (adaptive sampling)
   - Full step-level GPU kernel traces (PTX/cupti-level) and per-op GPU timelines
   - Full request payloads and user prompt text (redaction rules apply)

Sampling strategy overview
--------------------------
We use a hybrid deterministic+adaptive sampling strategy: a low base sample rate plus deterministic upsampling for classes of requests that historically produce high-value signals.

Base rates (default global policy)
- Trace sampling (end-to-end request spans): 1 in 200 requests (0.5%)
- Kernel-level detailed tracing: 1 in 10,000 requests (0.01%)
- Heavy payload capture (prompts > 2k tokens): 1 in 500 requests (0.2%)

Deterministic upsampling rules (always evaluated before random sampling)
1) Canary/experiment routes: 100% tracing for canary cohorts during rollout window.
2) Error-class upsampling: any request with status != 200 is captured at 100% for at least 10 minutes after first occurrence, then decays to base rate over an hour.
3) Tail-latency upsampling: requests that exceed route p95 latency are marked for additional traces for the next N=100 matching requests.
4) High-cost models: model_variants with per-token cost > X (configurable) increase trace sample to 1% by default.

Adaptive, cost-aware throttling
------------------------------
- Observability budget: each runtime cluster (per-region) has a monthly ingestion budget measured in "trace-equivalent-units" (TEUs). TEU is defined as a weighted unit that normalizes traces, kernel traces, and payload captures.
- When projected weekly TEU consumption reaches 60% of budget, the system reduces non-essential sampling rates by 30% and notifies owners. At 85% projected consumption, further reductions occur and only high-priority deterministic sampling remains.
- An emergency override allows SRE to enable 100% tracing for up to 2 hours for incident triage; this must be logged and tagged to an incident ID.

Retention and storage tiers
--------------------------
- Hot (7 days): full-span traces and per-request metadata stored in tracing backend (used for immediate triage and dashboards).
- Warm (30 days): aggregated histograms and reduced traces (kept with sampling metadata).
- Cold (365 days): token counters, aggregate model_variants cost metrics, and sampling logs for audit.

Table: storage and retention
| signal_type | retention | storage_location | downstream_exports |
| trace_full | 7d | trace-cluster-hot | alerting/dashboards |
| trace_reduced | 30d | trace-cluster-warm | performance-reports |
| aggregates | 365d | metrics-db | billing/simulation |

Dashboarding and alerting
-------------------------
- Critical SLO dashboards should use sampled-corrected histograms. Sampling-corrected estimators must be applied to p95/p99 calculations when sampling != 100%.
- Alerts:
  - Incoming trace TEU rate > cluster budget_projection_rate * 1.2 -> paged to eng-sre.
  - Spike in kernel-level error rate (>=5% of kernel calls in 10m) -> pager.
  - Sampling configuration drift (any change to deterministic rules) -> notify runtime config-owners and security for scrutiny.

Operational runbook (when more fidelity is needed)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Triage phase: Validate the failure mode using existing traces and aggregated metrics.
2) If insufficient signal, escalate to temporary upsampling: update cluster sampling override policy to increase trace sampling to 5% for affected routes for a maximum of 90 minutes.
3) If kernel-level detail required, enable kernel-level tracing for a dedicated rolling node pool with isolated TEU accounting.
4) After capture: revert overrides, tag traces with incident ID, and run cost reconciliation.
5) Produce a post-incident note listing why higher fidelity was required and whether sampling policies should be adjusted.

Change management and rollout process
-----------------------------------
- Sampling policy lives in a declarative feature flag repo: repo: infra/observability/sampling-policies, file: runtime-defaults.yaml.
- Changes require:
  1) Design doc (1 page) describing reason and measurement plan.
  2) PR with unit tests + simulation against synthetic workloads (see tools/telemetry-sim).
  3) Canaried rollout to 2% of clusters for 24 hours; check TEU impact and correctness.
  4) Gradual rollout with metric-based gates.

Config examples
---------------
YAML example for route-level policy (runtime-defaults.yaml excerpt):

---
routes:
  - name: /v1/generate
    default_trace_sample: 0.005 # 0.5%
    upsample_rules:
      - name: canary_cohort
        matcher: "route:generate AND cohort:canary"
        sample: 1.0
      - name: tail_latency_boost
        matcher: "route:generate AND latency>p95"
        sample: 0.2

CLI snippet: enable temporary override
$ ri telemetry override set --cluster=us-west-2 --trace-sample=0.05 --duration=90m --reason="incident-INC-1234"

Example queries (Appendix)
--------------------------
- Estimate true p95 from sampled histograms: use the per-bin weight correction factor included in each span (example SQL-like pseudocode):
  SELECT corrected_percentile(histogram_bins, sample_rate) FROM traces WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND ts BETWEEN ...;
- TEU projection snippet (pseudocode):
  projected_teu = current_week_teu + (average_daily_teu * remaining_days)

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Policy owner: Priya Nair (runtime-observability)
- On-call for telemetry ingestion: eng-sre on-call (pager duty team: infra-sre)
- Budget owner: Finance-ML (for cross-checks and chargebacks)

Appendix: privacy and redaction rules
------------------------------------
- No full prompt text is stored in hot traces by default. Prompts are redacted at capture time using redaction ruleset v2. See infra/observability/redaction-rules.md.
- PII found during capture triggers immediate encryption with customer-specific KMS per Private deployment and will be excluded from exported datasets.

Appendix: quick checklist for a high-fidelity capture request
-------------------------------------------------------------
1) Create a short incident doc and assign incident ID.
2) Open PR in infra/observability with sampling override.
3) Confirm TEU budget availability with eng-sre.
4) Apply override and monitor TEU spikes for first 5 minutes.
5) Revert and annotate results.
